solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I would like to be understood — warning from the clue here?

definitions.text: I would like to be understood
definitions.meaning: a plea not to be misinterpreted, said before a remark that might cause offence
the clue itself cautions the solver against a wrong reading, as any crossword clue tempts one

explanation.surface: Someone anxious to be understood, then a wink at the crossword clue itself issuing a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday idiom asking a listener not to misinterpret, and doubles as a caution a tricky clue might give its solver.

clue.text: Confused son avoids being on a bike maybe

indicators.note: the son keeps away from the word, so his letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a cyclist sits on the saddle, so is saddled, as a rider on a horse is

explanation.surface: A muddled boy who won't get on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saddled' here is taken literally as sitting in a saddle, with 'maybe' admitting a bike is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled is a synonym of muddled or befuddled, describing a mind that cannot think straight.

clue.text: What could make for an iron fist in naval punishment

definitions.text: What could make for an iron fist
definitions.meaning: an armoured glove of steel plates covers the hand of a knight
running a double line of sailors who struck the offender was a punishment at sea

explanation.surface: Harsh discipline at sea, ruled with an iron fist.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured glove is a gauntlet, and running the gauntlet between rows of men with ropes was a punishment in the navy.

clue.text: I'm poser maybe in act of betrayal

parts.note: the letters of 'I'm poser' are a jumbled pledge, so they are that pledge broken up, 'maybe' marking one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-confessed fraud admits a betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: Think of the answer as wordplay: 'broken' would signal an anagram, and the pledge word rearranged gives IMPOSER, the clue's 'I'm poser'; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to keep one's word to someone is a form of betrayal of the trust they placed in it.

clue.text: Sprinkler? The latest thing for safety in various shops

indicators.note: the end letter of safety goes inside the rearranged letters
various suggests the shops letters appear in assorted arrangements
the latest thing of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A sprinkler system as the latest safety feature in different shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The latest thing' looks like a fashion; it means the last letter, Y, which goes inside SHOPS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of the hyssop herb was used in ancient ritual to sprinkle water or blood, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Display revolutionary murderer as one devil-possessed

parts.note: a demo is a display or demonstration of something

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer

explanation.surface: A demonstration staged by a murderous revolutionary who seems possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks political, but it is the reversal signal; the murderer is the biblical first killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoniac is a person believed to be in the grip of an evil spirit.

clue.text: Unexpected holiday with bishop ousting one devil

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement of letters is a surprising reordering of them
the bishop's letters push out and take the place of the letter for one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A surprise holiday where a bishop throws out a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' is usually B in crosswords; here it is Right Reverend, a bishop's title, and the swap is made before the letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Harry is a traditional nickname for Satan, like Old Nick.

clue.text: Gosh, Will appears in emphatic personal form!

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh!
Will Self is an English novelist and journalist

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a man called Will shows up in his most forceful guise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like resolve; it is the writer Will Self.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-person reflexive pronoun is used to add emphasis, as in 'I did it on my own'.

clue.text: Cricketer awfully defiant rude, me? That's about right!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the letter for right
awfully suggests the words are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is defiant and rude, asking if that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Trueman was a famously blunt Yorkshire and England fast bowler of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Trueman was a celebrated English fast bowler, the first to take 300 Test wickets.

clue.text: Nasty spy Carl and I work in code-breaking

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A nasty spy and a colleague called Carl working together in cryptography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' reads as a description of the spy, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptanalysis is the study and practice of deciphering codes without the key.

clue.text: One to grab cards left on table

definitions.meaning: a bird of prey's hooked claw grips its catch
in card games the stock left after dealing is placed face down on the table

explanation.surface: Someone snatching up the cards left lying on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw seizes prey, and in games like patience the undealt stock pile has the same name.

clue.text: Checks quality of sound for audience — it is hard and "edgy"

indicators.note: an audience hears, so the words are rendered as they sound to listeners

parts.note: checks means curbs and quality of sound means tone

explanation.surface: A sound engineer checking tone for an audience, with an edgy hardness.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a kerb is the raised edge of a pavement, spelt differently from curb meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone forming the raised edge of a road is hard and literally forms an edge, hence the quotation marks.

clue.text: One lied to misrepresent image

indicators.note: misrepresenting something gives it a distorted form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter's slip: the letters of 'One lied' as printed have a second E where the answer needs a second O, so one E is read as O

explanation.surface: Someone lying to give a false image of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To misrepresent' signals the anagram, but the fodder as printed has ONELIED, which has an E where the answer needs a second O; the setter has slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: An eidolon is a phantom or idealised figure, an image or apparition of a person.

clue.text: The old man confused under the influence of drug

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, one's old man
pied type in printing is type jumbled up, so pied means confused

explanation.surface: A father befuddled by a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium comes from the poppy, so someone poppied is drowsy or stupefied as if drugged with it.

clue.text: Diplomat who could conjure up theatrical amity

indicators.note: conjuring up summons something new out of the given words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat able to put on a show of friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical amity' looks like a description of fake diplomatic friendliness; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer attached to an embassy to advise on defence matters holds diplomatic status.

clue.text: Sweet tablet in few drops of water, say, going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the built word is read in reverse
the tablet goes inside the water

parts.note: a pool is a small body of liquid, such as a puddle of spilt water
a pill is a medicinal tablet

explanation.surface: A pill dissolved in a little water, going down the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Few drops of water, say' is a puddle-sized pool; the container is built first and only then read backwards, as 'going the wrong way' applies to the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a boiled sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Bear wandering about in wood gets opportunity for refreshment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical wood

indicators.note: something wandering about moves around unpredictably, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear roaming in the woods finds a chance for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal in the wood, but it is only anagram fodder; 'wandering about' scrambles it to ABRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause from work for a cup of tea is a chance for refreshment, a British workplace custom.

clue.text: Something elemental that brings two animals together

parts.note: the first animal is a wolf
the second animal is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: An elemental force that unites two creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a chemical element, hence 'elemental'.

clue.text: Island's coloniser

definitions.meaning: the possessive reads as 'island is': a Greek island in the Dodecanese
Cecil ... was a British empire-builder in southern Africa

explanation.surface: The man who settled an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island, and Cecil Rhodes colonised the African territory once named Rhodesia after him.

clue.text: A friend you are texting no real expert?

parts.note: mate is British informal for friend
in text-message shorthand 'you are' becomes UR

explanation.surface: Texting a pal to ask if they are really no expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love rather than as a trained professional, so is not a genuine specialist.

clue.text: Greek community detectives going across lake

parts.note: EU, the European Union, was earlier the European Community

indicators.note: the detectives stretch across the lake, enclosing its letter

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives from a Greek community crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was an ancient Greek mathematician, the father of geometry.

clue.text: Drunk moonily engaging us in a threatening manner?

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the other word
a drunk word staggers about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk person, mooning about, approaches us in a menacing way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominously means in a way that bodes ill, suggesting a threat to come.

clue.text: Search in front of restaurant by city church

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A search outside a restaurant next to a city church.
explanation.walkthrough: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is British informal for a scouting look round.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance is an exploratory survey of an area, a kind of search.

clue.text: One to exude warmth, you might think — or scowl

definitions.text: One to exude warmth, you might think
definitions.meaning: taken literally, something that glows gives off warm light
to scowl is to stare angrily

explanation.surface: Someone you'd expect to radiate warmth, or else frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as glow-er it would be a radiator of warmth; in fact it means an angry stare.

clue.text: I'm a native terribly short of energy — chemical required by body

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged
being short of something means lacking it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A native person who is terribly low on energy needs a nutrient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of energy' removes E from NATIVE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin A is an essential nutrient the body needs for vision and growth.
